shared.studio: An independent design and development studio
shared.contactCopy: Tell me what you are launching or would like to change. I read every enquiry myself, ask questions and suggest the next step.

index.label: Websites, end to end
title: Websites,
end to end
index.intro: I'm Anton, a designer, developer and the founder of KADO. I create websites for businesses and SaaS products, from structure and visual direction to development, launch and ongoing support.
index.statementCopy: I lead both design and development. Early decisions account for how the website will work, and implementation preserves its character. You work directly with the person responsible for the project.
index.scopeIntro: We start with what your business needs today. That gives us the website format and the scope of work.

scope.title: Business website
scope.text: Services, projects and company information in a connected structure. Help visitors find what they need and understand why they should get in touch.

scope.title: Landing page
scope.text: One product, service or launch. A clear sequence that explains the offer and leads to an enquiry, booking or another relevant action.

scope.title: Website redesign
scope.text: For a business that has outgrown its website. Review the existing structure, update its presentation and decide what is worth keeping.

index.processIntro: Each stage produces something you can see and discuss. Your input matters when sharing context, preparing materials and reviewing decisions.

steps.title: Understand the project
steps.text: We discuss the business, audience and constraints, then define the scope, budget and timeline expectations.

steps.title: Build the structure and direction
steps.text: I present the page structure and visual direction, then develop the agreed approach across the website and mobile layouts.

steps.title: Turn design into a website
steps.text: I build the interface, forms and agreed functionality. Behaviour and performance are checked in the working build.

steps.title: Test and launch
steps.text: I check the main user journeys and publish the website. We discuss content updates and ongoing support.

projects.text: A venue's atmosphere, menu and booking journey. Art direction, UX/UI and an end-to-end website.
A brand story in horizontal motion. Art direction, web design, frontend and interactive animation.

index.pricingIntro: Structure, content readiness, visual assets and functionality shape the estimate. These starting points help you understand the scale before we talk.

pricing.title: Compact website
pricing.detail: From 4 weeks. Defined content, a focused structure and a limited number of complex interactions.

pricing.title: Bespoke website
pricing.detail: From 2 months. Discovery, structure, art direction, individual design and development.

faq.question: What should I prepare before getting in touch?
faq.answer: A short description of your business and project is enough. Share your current website, copy, photos or brand guidelines if available. We will identify what else is needed.

faq.question: Can you work from an existing design?
faq.answer: Yes. I review the layouts and intended behaviour before estimating development, responsive implementation and launch.

faq.question: Who prepares the copy and images?
faq.answer: We agree this at the start. We can use your existing materials or involve a suitable specialist. Copywriting, photography and complex visual assets are accounted for in the scope.

faq.question: What happens after launch?
faq.answer: I can continue supporting the website, updating content, adding pages and developing functionality. We agree the tasks and scope separately.

seo.title: Bespoke Website Design and Development | KADO
seo.description: Anton, founder of KADO: website structure, design and development for businesses and SaaS products. Explore the work, process, budgets and ongoing support.

redesign.label: Website redesign
title: Website
redesign
redesign.intro: Your business has changed, but the website has stayed behind. I review its structure, presentation and technical constraints, identify what is worth keeping and rebuild the rest around your needs.
redesign.statementCopy: An update starts with understanding what already works. Existing content, page addresses and familiar user journeys should be considered before the new design takes shape.
redesign.scopeIntro: A redesign can involve individual pages or an entire website. Reviewing the current version gives us the scope.

scope.title: Structure and content
scope.text: Rework navigation, introduce new services and remove outdated material so visitors can understand the offer more easily.

scope.title: Visual language
scope.text: Bring the website closer to the character of the business through composition, typography, imagery and mobile layouts.

scope.title: Implementation and migration
scope.text: Choose a suitable technical foundation. Account for content migration, forms, integrations and changes to page addresses.

redesign.processIntro: A link to your current website and a short description are a useful starting point. We assess the existing platform and functionality before estimating the work.

steps.title: Review the existing website
steps.text: I examine pages, navigation and key journeys. We discuss what has changed in the business and what needs improving.

steps.title: Plan the update
steps.text: We decide what to retain and what to rebuild. I develop the structure and visual direction for the new version.

steps.title: Design and develop
steps.text: I build the new pages and agreed functionality. Content and integrations are migrated within the defined scope.

steps.title: Move to the new version
steps.text: I check forms, links and mobile behaviour. Changes to URLs require a migration map and redirects.

projects.text: Structure, atmosphere and menu and booking journeys. An end-to-end website project.
A connected catalogue system. Logo, UX/UI, design system and checkout design.

redesign.pricingIntro: A new homepage and a full rebuild with data migration require different scopes of work. I start with your current version and its constraints.

pricing.title: Estimated after a website review
pricing.detail: Page types, content, platform, integrations and migration determine the budget and timeline.

faq.question: Does the whole website need rebuilding?
faq.answer: Not always. Changes to a few page structures or their presentation may be enough. The review helps establish what is needed.

faq.question: Can we keep the existing platform?
faq.answer: That depends on its condition and the changes required. I assess the constraints and feasibility before committing to a particular platform.

faq.question: What happens to search rankings?
faq.answer: Existing URLs, content and metadata need consideration, with redirects where addresses change. A redesign can affect rankings; a loss-free migration cannot be guaranteed in advance.

faq.question: What do you need to get started?
faq.answer: Send the website address and a few sentences about the changes you want. We can discuss source files, access and analytics at the next step.

seo.title: Website Redesign — Structure, Design and Development | KADO
seo.description: Update your existing website with Anton, founder of KADO. Structure review, new design, development and migration planning, with a scope-based estimate.

corporate.label: Business website
title: Business
websites
corporate.intro: A website where clients can understand your services, explore your work and get in touch. I lead structure, design and development so every page belongs to the same visual system.
corporate.statementCopy: A service page, a case study and a company story need different presentations. Shared composition and navigation principles connect them into a website that is easy to explore and expand.
corporate.scopeIntro: A multi-page website suits businesses with several services, different audiences and content that needs space of its own.

scope.title: Services and business areas
scope.text: Dedicated pages for substantial offers, explaining scope, conditions and examples with a clear way to get in touch.

scope.title: Projects and experience
scope.text: Work, decisions and company information that help visitors assess experience relevant to their project.

scope.title: Content and future growth
scope.text: Plan who will update content and how. Account for new services, projects and language versions.

corporate.processIntro: We begin with the content map and visitor journeys. The business needs determine the number of pages.

steps.title: Understand the business
steps.text: We discuss services, audiences and materials, defining who the website is for and what they need to know.

steps.title: Design the structure
steps.text: I map the pages and their content. Key screens establish the visual direction and navigation principles.

steps.title: Build the system
steps.text: I develop page types and responsive interfaces. Content management and integrations follow the actual requirements.

steps.title: Prepare for use
steps.text: I check links, forms and mobile journeys, prepare the pages for indexing and publish the website.

projects.text: Sections connected by the venue's atmosphere and visitor needs. Art direction, UX/UI and end-to-end delivery.
Consistent logic across different catalogues. Logo, UX/UI and design system work.

corporate.pricingIntro: Distinct page types, content readiness, content management and external services all shape the scope.

pricing.title: Business website
pricing.detail: The budget and timeline follow the agreed structure and functionality. Catalogues, integrations and language versions are included in the assessment.

faq.question: How many pages does a business need?
faq.answer: Enough to explain its offers and support visitor needs. We start with which services to describe, projects to show and actions to make possible.

faq.question: Can we add services and projects later?
faq.answer: Yes. We should plan this in the structure and content management approach, including which sections will change and who will update them.

faq.question: Is content preparation included?
faq.answer: We assess your existing materials and identify what is missing. Copy, photography, illustration and complex graphics are accounted for separately in the scope.

faq.question: Can the website include a catalogue or an account area?
faq.answer: These features need their own assessment. Their journeys, data and constraints are not automatically included in every business website.

seo.title: Business Website Design and Development | KADO
seo.description: An individual website for your company: services, projects, business information and enquiry forms. Structure, design, development and support by Anton at KADO.

landing.label: Landing pages
title: Landing page
development
landing.intro: A page for one offer: a product, service or launch. I shape the story, create an individual design and build a website around the action your project needs.
landing.statementCopy: A landing page answers the visitor's questions in sequence: what you offer, whether it suits them, the conditions and how to start. The visual idea supports that sequence.
landing.scopeIntro: Landing pages suit individual services, products, events and campaigns. The content depends on who visits and where they come from.

scope.title: The offer and its evidence
scope.text: Explain the substance, show the conditions and answer questions that arise before an enquiry. Define the relevant visitor action.

scope.title: Character and presentation
scope.text: Find a visual direction for the brand or product. Build typography, imagery and motion around the content.

scope.title: Development and launch
scope.text: Build a responsive page with the agreed forms and functionality. Check behaviour across screen sizes and publish it.

landing.processIntro: We start with the page's purpose and content. Sections and animation follow where they help explain the offer.

steps.title: Define the purpose
steps.text: We discuss the product, audience and traffic sources, then choose the action the page should support.

steps.title: Shape the story
steps.text: I organise the content and section order, propose a visual direction and develop it into the page design.

steps.title: Build the interface
steps.text: I create responsive layouts, forms and agreed interactions. Visual assets and integrations are scoped explicitly.

steps.title: Check and publish
steps.text: I test visitor actions, mobile behaviour and build performance, then launch the page and discuss future updates.

projects.text: Product and brand story in one continuous sequence. Design, frontend and interactive animation.
A product range centred on one object. Web design, 3D graphics and animation.

landing.pricingIntro: A page with ready content and a launch requiring copy development and 3D graphics involve different amounts of work.

pricing.title: Landing page, end to end
pricing.detail: We discuss the offer, content and functionality before setting a budget and timeline. Advertising spend is not included in the development price.

faq.question: When is a landing page enough?
faq.answer: When one offer can be explained around one primary action. A business with several services and substantial independent content may need a multi-page website.

faq.question: Does this include advertising?
faq.answer: I consider traffic sources when designing the page. Campaign setup and management need to be arranged with an advertising specialist.

faq.question: Can we add more pages later?
faq.answer: Yes. If expansion is planned, we should discuss it early and account for it in the structure. Additional pages are estimated by their content and functionality.

faq.question: What has the biggest effect on the budget?
faq.answer: Content readiness, design scope, illustration or 3D, forms and external integrations. The number of sections alone does not describe the work.

seo.title: Landing Page Design and Development | KADO
seo.description: A landing page for your product, service or launch: offer, structure, individual design, responsive development and enquiry forms. Explore the process at KADO.
